bull.b: Robust and expanding free cash flow shows that DoorDash’s profitability is translating into cash, giving it resources to fund technology, fulfillment, expansion and other strategic investments.

Rising subscription penetration can increase order frequency and gross profit per user, while expanding merchant tools deepen platform integration, improve retention and create additional recurring monetization opportunities.

Expansion beyond restaurants and stronger international operations diversify DoorDash’s revenue base, enlarge its addressable market and support longer-term order growth as consumers adopt delivery across more categories.

bear.b: Despite the profitability inflection, thin operating and net margins leave limited protection against delivery-cost inflation, competitive pressure or execution mistakes, making sustained margin expansion important to the long-term model.

Leverage remains manageable but has increased meaningfully, reducing financial flexibility relative to the prior balance sheet and increasing sensitivity to slower growth, margin compression or higher funding requirements.

DoorDash is pursuing several complex initiatives simultaneously, including autonomy and physical fulfillment. Delays, cost overruns or weak adoption could defer returns and pressure margins before the investments deliver scale benefits.
